SMTO-SKL-0184 — The Agent's GitHub request was incomplete or not allowed

GUID: e4b86db3-fdf4-5ced-b427-228fc5e08fd5
Slug: github-invalid-arguments
Domain: SKL · Subsystem: github

What happened

  • SMTO stopped the Agent's GitHub request before sending it, because something in it was missing, in the wrong form, or not supported. Nothing was sent to GitHub.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Tell the Agent the exact GitHub project (for example owner/name) and ask it to look the project up first. Any change on GitHub must be tied to a project the Agent has just looked up.
  2. Give the exact issue, pull request or release number, and any file path without shortcuts like ../. SMTO refuses vague targets and file paths that could point outside the intended folder.
  3. Ask the Agent to repeat the request. Nothing was sent to GitHub, so a corrected request is safe.

What success looks like

  • The Agent completes the GitHub request, or asks you to confirm a change before making it.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. The GitHub skill may not support this kind of request.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The GitHub skill rejected the call before contacting GitHub: arguments failed the tool's input validation, a path segment contained '.', '..' or control characters, the API path was malformed, or the operation is not supported.

What this means

  • Tool schema, method/path checks, segment validation or operation routing reject unsupported or unsafe arguments. This diagnostic adds no GitHub access. Inspect the original receipt and request stage before repeating work; preserve exact account, host, repository and object identities.

Why this can happen

  • Tool schema, method/path checks, segment validation or operation routing reject unsupported or unsafe arguments.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect bounded schema fields, safe path segments and required write account/repository IDs.

How to fix it

  • Compare the call with the tool's advertised input fields and use only those. Paths must not contain '.', '..' or control characters. Every write needs explicit account_ref/account_id, host, owner, repo and repository_id taken from a fresh github.repo read, plus the exact issue/PR/release number or ID.
  • Use bounded fields in the advertised schema. Writes require explicit account_ref/account_id, host, owner/repo and repository_id from github.repo.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect exact provider state and authority first.

How to verify the fix

  • Correct deliberate arguments target the exact confirmed resource.

What not to do

  • Do not expose secrets or blindly replay uncertain mutations.

Technical notes

  • This diagnostic adds no GitHub access. Inspect the original receipt and request stage before repeating work; preserve exact account, host, repository and object identities.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
